questions.question: In the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), what is the specific purpose of a WARNING statement?

options.a: To provide additional helpful information for a specific task
options.b: To call attention to materials or processes that must be followed to avoid injury or death
options.c: To identify methods that prevent damage to the aircraft structure

questions.justification: The AMM safety terminology defines a WARNING as calling attention to the use of material, processes, methods, or limits which must be followed precisely to avoid injury or death to persons.

questions.question: In the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), what does a CAUTION statement indicate?

options.a: Methods and procedures that must be followed to avoid damage to equipment
options.b: Actions that require immediate evacuation of the hangar
options.c: The start of a safety-critical structural inspection

questions.justification: According to the manual, a CAUTION calls attention to methods and procedures which must be followed to avoid damage to equipment.

questions.question: What is the general maintenance principle regarding safety instructions found in the AMM?

options.a: They are only mandatory during heavy maintenance checks
options.b: They must be obeyed at all times to prevent injury to persons and damage to the aircraft
options.c: They serve as guidelines that can be modified by the lead engineer

questions.justification: The document states: 'When you work on aircraft, make sure that you obey all the AMM safety procedures. This will prevent injury to persons and/or damage to the aircraft.'

questions.question: How are safety instructions integrated within the procedural steps of the AMM?

options.a: They are only listed in Chapter 00 of the manual
options.b: They are repeated as necessary in the particular step of the operation to which they apply
options.c: They are provided only on external aircraft placards

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Caution and warnings are repeated as necessary in the particular step of the towing operation [or other tasks] to which they apply.'

questions.question: Which visual indicator is used in the training manual to differentiate between a WARNING and a CAUTION?

options.a: Warnings are in red boxes; Cautions are in orange/yellow boxes
options.b: Warnings are in bold text; Cautions are in italics
options.c: Warnings use the letter 'W'; Cautions use the letter 'C'

questions.justification: The graphic representation on page 208 shows WARNING labels in red and CAUTION labels in orange/yellow.

questions.question: When performing a task that involves chemical etching, which safety designator would likely appear in the AMM?

options.b: CAUTION

questions.justification: Since chemical etching involves the 'use of material, processes, methods' that could be hazardous to humans if not followed precisely, it falls under the definition of a WARNING.

questions.question: A procedure specifies a torque limit for a non-structural bolt. Failure to follow this limit would damage the bolt threads but not cause injury. How would this limit be categorized?

options.b: CAUTION

questions.justification: A CAUTION is defined as calling attention to limits 'which must be followed to avoid damage to equipment.'

questions.question: If a task in the AMM refers to 'Safety Data', what type of information is typically included?

options.b: Placards and markings including WARNINGS and CAUTIONS

questions.justification: Under ATA 11 (General), the manual states that 'Safety Data' placards and markings include 'WARNINGS and CAUTIONS.'

questions.question: During aircraft jacking, if the technician fails to point the aircraft upwind, which safety designator is violated according to Chapter 07?

options.b: WARNING

questions.justification: Tasks involving physical aircraft safety and equipment orientation (like jacking) that prevent damage to the structure or jacks are generally preceded by CAUTIONS in the Airbus AMM framework.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a WARNING application mentioned in the manual during door operations?

options.a: Checking the nitrogen pressure on the cylinder
options.b: Avoiding explosive decompression by not opening a pressurized door
options.c: Setting the door handle to the LOCKED position

questions.justification: The manual specifically uses a WARNING label for opening pressure-sealed doors when the aircraft is pressurized, as this can cause 'explosive decompression, kill or cause injury.'

questions.question: What does a 'Customized Manual' contain in the Airbus documentation system?

options.a: Generic information applicable to all aircraft manufacturers
options.b: Information applicable only to a particular airline or group of operators
options.c: A list of every part ever manufactured by Airbus

questions.justification: The document defines a customized manual as one that 'contains only the information applicable to a particular airline or a group of operators.'

questions.question: How is a non-customized manual referred to when it is applicable to only one specific aircraft model, such as the A320 only?

options.b: ENVELOPE

questions.justification: A non-customized manual is called ENVELOPE when 'the information is applicable to only one specific aircraft model / type / serie. (I.e.: A320 only)'.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a GENERIC and an ENVELOPE non-customized manual?

options.a: Generic is for all Airbus types, while Envelope is for one specific model
options.b: Generic is printed on paper, while Envelope is on CD-ROM
options.c: Generic contains B1 data, while Envelope contains B2 data

questions.justification: The text states Generic is applicable to all aircraft models/types/series (e.g., all Airbus types), whereas Envelope is for only one specific model (e.g., A320 only).

questions.question: In the Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC), what nomenclature indicates a part is specific to a customized layout?

options.b: A variant item number that includes the customized nomenclature

questions.justification: The IPC Customization section states: 'The customized nomenclature contains a variant item number, only the basic item number is illustrated.'

questions.question: What does the note 'MISSING ITEMS AND VARIANTS ARE NOT APPLICABLE' in an IPC list signify?

options.a: The page is missing from the manual
options.b: The items are not used on that specific customer's aircraft
options.c: The parts must be ordered as a special request

questions.justification: This note is used in customized IPCs as a reminder to avoid concern over items or variants not applicable to that specific customer.

questions.question: When using a global IPC (AIB), which aircraft does the information relate to?

options.b: All aircraft without specific customer information

questions.justification: The IPC customization note says: 'The global IPC (AIB) contains information relating to all A/C without specific customer information.'

questions.question: A technician is checking part numbers for a fleet of mixed Airbus types. Which non-customized manual type should they use for commonality data across all types?

options.b: GENERIC

questions.justification: A GENERIC manual is applicable to all aircraft models/types/series (all AIRBUS types).

questions.question: Where will the customer code and revision date appear in a customized IPC?

options.b: At the bottom of each page
options.c: On the cover of the CD-ROM

questions.justification: The document specifies: 'The customer code and the revision date will appear at the bottom of each page.'

questions.question: How is the applicability of a specific part number to an aircraft confirmed in a customized manual?

options.a: By referencing the 'Effectivity' or 'MSN' column in the detailed part list
options.b: By checking the color of the manual page
options.c: By contacting the local airport authority

questions.justification: Customized manuals contain information applicable to a particular airline; for specific parts, the effectivity/MSN cross-reference is the standard method used in the IPC and AMM.

questions.question: Which document allows the technician to find specific part numbers for line replaceable aircraft units?

options.b: IPC

questions.justification: The IPC (Illustrated Parts Catalog) is intended for use in identifying, provisioning, and issuing line replaceable aircraft parts.

questions.question: What are the two types of revisions provided for Airbus technical publications?

options.b: Normal and Temporary

questions.justification: The manual states: 'There are two types of revisions: normal and temporary.'

questions.question: How are temporary revisions visually identified in paper or digital format?

options.a: They are on blue pages or in blue text
options.b: They are on yellow pages or on yellow diskettes

questions.justification: The document specifies: 'Temporary revisions... are on yellow pages or on yellow diskettes.'

questions.question: What is the scheduling basis for 'Normal Revisions'?

options.a: They are released after every aircraft accident
options.b: They are calendar scheduled
options.c: They are issued only upon airline request

questions.justification: The manual states: 'normal revisions are calendar scheduled.'

questions.question: When are 'Temporary Revisions' utilized in the documentation system?

options.b: For urgent information requiring immediate attention or advanced notification
options.c: To provide translated versions of the manual

questions.justification: Temporary revisions 'are used for urgent information requiring immediate attention or advanced notification.'

questions.question: Which media can be used to provide Airbus Technical Publications to operators?

options.b: CD-ROMs, 16mm cassettes, Magnetic tapes, and Paper documents

questions.justification: The 'MEDIA' diagram identifies Paper documents, Magnetic tapes, CD-ROMs, 16mm cassettes, Microfiches, and Diskettes.

questions.question: What is the official reference language for the Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM)?

options.a: The language of the country where the aircraft is registered
options.b: The original English language version produced by AIRBUS
options.c: French, as Airbus is headquartered in Toulouse

questions.justification: The manual states: 'If any or all of the AMM is translated, the official version shall be the original English language version produced by AIRBUS.'

questions.question: If a technician finds a conflict between a temporary revision and a normal revision, which should take precedence?

options.a: The Normal Revision, as it is the permanent record
options.b: The Temporary Revision, as it contains urgent information
options.c: Neither; they must contact Airbus for clarification

questions.justification: Temporary revisions are for 'urgent information requiring immediate attention.' In aviation documentation, the temporary revision always overrides the existing data until it is incorporated into a normal revision.

questions.question: Where can a record of all approved SRM revisions be found?

options.b: In the front pages of the SRM
options.c: On the FAP door status page

questions.justification: The manual states the SRM front pages include a 'record of revisions approved.'

questions.question: How are measurement systems handled in AIRBUS Technical Publications?

options.b: Both metric and non-metric are used, with the original reference quoted first
options.c: Only US units are used for all global operators

questions.justification: The document states: 'AIRBUS Technical Publications use both metric and non-metric... The system used in the original reference documents is quoted first, followed by the conversion... in brackets.'

questions.question: Which document lists the 'Highlights' and 'Record of Revisions' at its beginning?

options.b: SRM

questions.justification: The SRM manual breakdown states: 'The manual also contains... some additional information pages (HIGHLIGHTS, RECORD OF REVISIONS...) at the beginning of the manual.'

questions.question: What is the maximum aircraft weight allowed for lifting at the landing gears for a wheel change?

options.b: Maximum Take-Off Weight (MTOW)

questions.justification: The manual states: 'The aircraft can be lifted at the landing gears up to its max. weight to change wheels.' This refers to the MTOW.

questions.question: Which safety pins must be confirmed in position before lifting the landing gear?

options.b: The ground safety locks

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Make sure that the ground safety locks are in position an (on) the landing gears.'

questions.question: From which direction should hydraulic jacks be positioned for landing gear lifting?

options.b: From behind

questions.justification: The manual specifies: 'The hydraulic jacks have to be positioned from behind to prevent damage to the sensors of the weight and balance system.'

questions.question: What is the status of the parking brake required during landing gear lifting?

options.b: It must be released

questions.justification: The manual instructions for landing gear lifting state: 'Make sure that the parking brake is released.'

questions.question: What mandatory action is required if a landing gear is accidentally lifted outside of the designated ball pad?

options.b: Landing gear change

questions.justification: The manual warns: 'Never lift the landing gear outside of the ball pad, severe damage to the landing gear makes gear change mandatory.'

questions.question: What specific tool is required when jacking the nose landing gear?

options.b: A nose landing gear jack adapter

questions.justification: The instructions state: 'use the right nose landing gear jack adapter and install that tool correct.'

questions.question: Why is the positioning of the jack from behind critical for the weight and balance system?

options.a: It prevents bending the tire stem
options.b: It prevents damage to the system sensors
options.c: It allows the ground safety locks to be reached

questions.justification: The manual says positioning from behind is necessary 'to prevent damage to the sensors of the weight and balance system.'

questions.question: On the NLG and MLG jacking diagrams, what part of the gear serves as the primary contact point for the jack?

options.b: The ball pad / jacking point

questions.justification: The jacking diagrams identify the 'JACKING POINT' or 'JACK ADAPTER WITH BALL PAD' as the contact location.

questions.question: During a wheel change, what must be done with the ground safety locks?

options.a: They must be removed to allow axle travel
options.b: They must be in position on the landing gears
options.c: They are only required for main jacking, not wheel changes

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Make sure that the ground safety locks are in position' for landing gear lifting tasks.

questions.question: Which document should be referred to for detailed information on 'Shoring' the aircraft?

options.b: The AMM

questions.justification: Under section 07-20, the document simply says: 'Shoring see AMM.'

questions.question: Where is the built-in aircraft trim indicator located for performing a quick leveling check?

options.b: Near the refuel control panel in the right wing root

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Quick leveling check can be carried out using the build in aircraft trim indicator near the refuel control panel in the right wing root.'

questions.question: What equipment is used when 'Precision Trimming' is required for the aircraft?

options.b: Sight tubes, sighting rods, and a theodolite

questions.justification: The manual specifies: 'Precision trimming must be done by means of sight tubes, sighting rods and a theodolite.'

questions.question: At which position on the built-in indicator grid is the aircraft considered to be in the zero position for both pitch and roll?

options.b: D4

questions.justification: The manual states: 'The aircraft is in the zero position in pitch and roll, when the bubble is at the D4 position.'

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of weighing the aircraft at defined intervals?

options.b: To determine the dry operating weight and center of gravity
options.c: To calculate the fuel load for the next flight

questions.justification: The document states: 'Aircraft weighing is performed... in order to determine the dry operating weight... The weight is used to determine the center of gravity.'

questions.question: Where are special weighing platforms placed during the aircraft weighing process?

options.a: Inside the cabin along the center aisle
options.b: At the normal lifting positions

questions.justification: The manual specifies: 'Special weighing platforms are used at the normal lifting positions for this task.'

questions.question: Based on the Leveling Indicator diagram, what is the dimension of each square in the D4 grid?

options.b: 0.5 inches

questions.justification: The LEVELING INDICATOR diagram (page 158) labels the grid spacing as '0.5"'.

questions.question: If the leveling bubble is at position B2, what does this indicate about the aircraft's attitude?

options.b: The aircraft is not in the zero position for pitch and/or roll
options.c: The aircraft weight exceeds the jack capacity

questions.justification: Since zero position is defined specifically as D4, any other position like B2 indicates the aircraft is not level.

questions.question: Which axis is being checked when observing the bubble movement along the 'A to G' axis of the leveling indicator?

options.b: Pitch axis

questions.justification: The indicator grid has numbered columns (1-7) and lettered rows (A-G). Based on standard leveling indicator orientation in the wing root (longitudinal), rows A-G typically correspond to pitch adjustments.

questions.question: Where can a spirit level be used as an alternative for a leveling check?

options.a: In the FWD Cargo Compartment or Passenger compartment
options.b: On the top of the vertical stabilizer

questions.justification: The Jacking section (ATA 07) lists alternative leveling check methods, including 'a Spirit Level in the FWD Cargo Compartment or in the Passenger compartment.'

questions.question: What is the status of the weight variants during a weighing operation?

options.a: The aircraft must be weighed in its 'at delivery' configuration
options.b: The operation determines the 'dry operating weight' of the individual aircraft
options.c: Fuel must be at 50% capacity for a valid weighing

questions.justification: The manual states weighing is performed 'to determine the dry operating weight of the individual aircraft.'

questions.question: By which part of the aircraft can it be towed according to the training manual?

options.a: The nose landing gear or the main landing gear
options.b: The nose landing gear only

questions.justification: The document states: 'you can tow the aircraft by the nose landing gear or the main landing gear.'

questions.question: Is it permissible to tow the aircraft if it has deflated tires?

options.a: No, it must be jacked and tires changed first
options.b: Yes, you can tow the aircraft with deflated tires
options.c: Only if the aircraft is empty

questions.justification: The text states: 'You can also tow the aircraft with deflated tires.'

questions.question: What is a major difference between 'maintenance towing' and 'transportation servicing towing'?

options.a: Transportation servicing only involves moving aircraft for positioning or dispatch pushback
options.b: Maintenance towing requires a pilot in the cockpit at all times
options.c: Transportation servicing uses the yellow hydraulic hand pump

questions.justification: The manual states: 'The major differences between the two are that transportation services only get involved with moving aircraft on ramps for positioning or dispatch pushback.'

questions.question: Who is required on the aircraft brakes during transportation servicing towing?

options.b: A pilot or qualified maintenance man
options.c: A ground coordinator using a headset

questions.justification: The text states: 'When they are handling the towing operation, they require either a pilot or qualified maintenance man on the aircraft brakes.'

questions.question: In which document are the maintenance towing procedures specifically detailed?

options.b: Ramp Operation Manual

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Maintenance towing procedures are laid down in the applicable AMM - Chapter 09.'

questions.question: Which parameter defines the distance between the centerline of the aircraft's longitudinal axis and the theoretical center of turn?

options.b: Y

questions.justification: The Turning Radii section defines 'Y' as the 'distance between the centerline of the A/C longitudinal axis (X-axis) and the theoretical center of turn.'

questions.question: What does the dimension 'A' represent in the steering and turning radius diagram?

options.b: The minimum turning width for a 180° turn
options.c: The length of the tow bar

questions.justification: The manual states: '"A" matches the minimum turning width for a 180° turn.'

questions.question: What is the effective turn angle for an A320 when the steering angle is at its maximum 75°?
questions.justification: The Turning Radii table on page 166 shows that at 75° steering angle, the A320 has an EFFEC TURN of 70°.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered an 'abnormal situation' for maintenance towing?

options.b: Aircraft stuck in mud

questions.justification: The manual lists 'aircraft stuck in mud, towing with flat tires, engines removal' as examples of maintenance involvement in abnormal situations.

questions.question: According to the radii chart, which aircraft variant requires the largest minimum turning width (A) for a 180° turn?
questions.justification: The Turning Radii chart lists dimension 'A' for the A321 as 90'6" (27.6 m), which is larger than the A319 (67'8") and A320 (75'1").

questions.question: What is the maximum period covered by the 'parking aircraft in flight-ready condition' procedure?

options.b: Not more than 15 days

questions.justification: The Parking section states: 'The parking aircraft in flight-ready condition procedure for a period of not more than 15 days (Ref. AMM 10-11-00)...'

questions.question: What is the primary function of aircraft mooring?

options.a: To calibrate the weight and balance sensors
options.b: To prevent damage to the aircraft on ground in high wind conditions
options.c: To secure the aircraft during long-term storage of over 6 months

questions.justification: The manual states: 'The function of mooring, is to prevent damage to the aircraft on ground in high wind conditions.'

questions.question: At what intervals must periodic ground checks be performed during a 15-day parking period?

options.b: At 7 day intervals
options.c: Only once before return to operation

questions.justification: The manual lists: 'periodic ground checks during parking at 7 days intervals (Ref. AMM 10-11-00)'.

questions.question: According to the mooring limits, when is mooring NOT necessary for wind speeds less than 50 Kts?

options.a: If the aircraft is pointed downwind
options.b: If the aircraft configuration is within the limits of ATA 05-57-00
options.c: If the aircraft is parked in a hangar

questions.justification: The text states: 'For wind speeds less than 50 kts: mooring is not necessary if the aircraft configuration is in the limits given in chapter 05-57-00.'

questions.question: What is the orientation requirement for mooring if the aircraft points into the wind and speed is between 50 and 70 Kts?

options.b: Moor at the NLG and MLG
options.c: Moor at the tail jack only

questions.justification: The manual specifies: 'If the aircraft points into the wind and wind speed is: between 50 and 70 Kts, moor the aircraft at the NLG.'

questions.question: During the parking procedure, why must an access platform be kept at a sufficient distance from the aircraft?

options.a: To allow for wing thermal expansion
options.b: In wind, shock absorber rebound can cause movement of the aircraft
options.c: To prevent interference with the ADIRU alignment

questions.justification: A CAUTION in the Parking section states: 'KEEP THE ACCESS PLATFORM AT A SUFFICIENT DISTANCE... (IN WIND, SHOCK ABSORBER REBOUND CAN CAUSE MOVEMENT OF THE AIRCRAFT).'

questions.question: What mooring action is required if wind speeds or gusts exceed 50 Kts and the wind direction is NOT stable?

options.a: Moor the aircraft at the NLG only
options.b: Moor the aircraft at the NLG and the MLG
options.c: The aircraft must be moved into a hangar

questions.justification: The manual states: 'If the aircraft does not point into the wind or the direction of the wind is not stable: for wind speeds or gusts more than 50 Kts, moor the aircraft at the NLG and the MLG.'

questions.question: How many times can the 15-day 'flight-ready condition' parking procedure be renewed?

options.b: Only one more time

questions.justification: The document lists: 'renewal parking procedures for not more than 15 days only one more time (Ref. AMM 10-11-00)'.

questions.question: In the 'Aircraft Storage' procedure for 6 months, what are the specified periodic check intervals?

options.b: 7 days, 15 days, 1 month, and 3 months

questions.justification: The Storage section specifies: 'periodic ground checks during storage at 7 days interval, at 15 days interval, at 1 month interval and at 3 months interval'.

questions.question: What must be ensured regarding the landing gear before commencing a parking procedure?

options.a: The tires are inflated to maximum pressure
options.b: The gear ground is safetied, locking devices and wheel chocks are in position
options.c: The steering bypass pin is removed

questions.justification: The CAUTION in the Parking section states: 'MAKE SURE THAT THE LANDING GEAR GROUND IS SAFETIED, LOCKING DEVICES AND WHEEL CHOCKS ARE IN POSITION.'

questions.question: Which category of placards and markings is identified by the number '(1)' in AMM Chapter 11?

options.b: Maintenance Data

questions.justification: The manual states: 'By Local Regulation... When these types of placards are shown in Chapter 11, they are identified by (1).'

questions.question: What information is included in 'Safety Data' placards?

options.b: WARNINGS and CAUTIONS for flight crew and passenger cabins

questions.justification: Safety Data placards 'are used for the flight crew, and passenger cabins... They include WARNINGS and CAUTIONS.'

questions.question: What is the standard appearance of Type No. 1 and No. 2 labels?

options.b: Plastic material with white letters on black matt finish
options.c: Adhesive vinyl with red warning text

questions.justification: The manual states: 'Standard No. 1 and 2 labels are in plastic material with white letters on black matt finish.'

questions.question: Where are 'Type No. 3' FOTOFOIL labels specifically used on the aircraft?

options.a: Inside the cockpit on the overhead panel
options.b: In Skydrol zones

questions.justification: Type No. 3 labels are defined as metal foil 'for use in skydrol zones'.

questions.question: When an aircraft is fully painted, what color are the blanking patches on the hoisting points?

options.b: The same color as the adjacent area

questions.justification: The document states: 'Each blanking sheet is painted in the same color as the adjacent area.'

questions.question: What is the required height for letters identifying access panels and doors?

questions.question: According to the Electrical Identification code, what is the letter height used for 'CODE A' (in boxes and panels)?

questions.question: Which code and letter height is used for the identification of 'Racks, Boxes and Panels' (CODE C)?

questions.justification: The diagram labels CODE C (Racks, Boxes, and Panels) with a letter height of 6.4 mm (0.251 in.).

questions.question: What is the designated letter height for the identification of 'Hydraulic System Components' (CODE D)?
questions.justification: The chart labels CODE D (Hydraulic System Components) with a letter height of 4 mm (0.157 in.).

questions.question: Where is the primary reference for finding aircraft panel locations?

options.b: AMM Chapter 06

questions.justification: The manual states: 'For more information about panel location, refer to AMM Chapter 06. Use the AMM Chapter 06 as the primary reference.'

questions.question: Which component constitutes the 'Primary Structure' of the engine pylon?

options.c: The pylon to wing center fillets

questions.question: How many engine attachment points does the pylon provide?

questions.question: How is the pylon box primary structure physically attached to the wing?

options.a: By means of twelve high-tension bolts
options.b: At three attachment points
options.c: Through a single main support beam

questions.justification: The manual specifies the pylon box 'is attached to the wing at three points.'

questions.question: What are the main assembly components of the pylon box?

options.a: Ribs, two upper spars, and one lower spar
options.b: Monolithic skins and internal honeycomb core

questions.justification: The manual states: 'The pylon box is composed of ribs, two upper spars and one lower spar, and panels...'

questions.question: At which rib position is the forward pylon-to-wing attachment fitting located?

options.b: Rib 4

questions.justification: The Pylon to Wing Attachment section identifies: 'This fitting located at Rib 4 is made of titanium alloy and carries vertical loads.'

questions.question: Which structural member transmits engine thrust to the wing?

options.b: A spherical bearing transmitting thrust to a spigot bolted to the bottom wing skin
options.c: The four shingles on the forward fork

questions.justification: The manual specifies: 'Immediately behind the forward attach fitting a spherical bearing transmits the thrust to a spigot bolted to the bottom wing skin panel.'

questions.question: What is the material of the aft engine mount used on Single Aisle aircraft?

options.b: Inconel alloy

questions.justification: The diagram on page 585 identifies the 'ENGINE MOUNT' as being made of 'INCONEL ALLOY'.

questions.question: For the IAE V2500 engine configuration, at which rib is the aft engine-to-pylon mount located?

options.b: Rib 3

questions.justification: The manual states: 'At the aft engine to pylon attach fitting... located at Rib 3 for CFM 56-5... or at Rib 4 for IAE V2500 engine configuration.'

questions.question: Which pylon fitting is responsible for reacting to vertical loads, side loads, and roll movement?

options.b: The aft engine mount
options.c: The pylon to wing center fillets

questions.question: What is the primary function of the vent hole located in the inner pane of a cabin window assembly?

options.a: To allow condensation to drain into the fuselage skin

options.c: To provide a mounting point for the window retainer ring

questions.question: Which component is used to hold the cabin window panel assembly in position against the window frame?

options.b: Cruciform fitting

questions.justification: View A from the inside (page 1) shows the window panel assembly is held in position by a retainer ring secured by eye bolts and nuts.

questions.question: In the event of an outer pane failure in a cabin window, how is cabin pressure maintained?

options.a: By the automatic activation of the emergency decompression valves
options.b: By the inner pane which is designed to maintain full cabin pressure
options.c: By the window seal which expands to fill the gap left by the outer pane

questions.justification: The document states on page 3 that the inner pane is able to maintain the cabin pressure in case of outer pane failure.

questions.question: What material is used for the construction of the inner and outer panes of the aircraft windows?

options.b: Stretched acrylic

questions.justification: As per the structure layout description on page 3, the windows have inner and outer panes made of stretched acrylic.

questions.question: Why are circular windows installed in passenger/crew and emergency exit doors?

options.a: To allow the crew to inspect for smoke in the cargo compartments
options.b: To verify if the outside is clear for door opening or slide deployment
options.c: To allow passengers to check the status of the engine cowlings

questions.justification: Page 3 specifies that door windows are used for inspection and observation to check from the outside if the cabin is pressurized or to verify if the outside is clear for door opening/slide deployment.

questions.question: During a walkaround inspection, you notice a failure of the outer window pane. Based on the failsafe design, what is the structural consequence?

options.a: The aircraft is grounded as the inner pane cannot hold pressure for more than one flight cycle
options.b: The inner pane maintains cabin pressure, allowing for continued operation under specific maintenance conditions
options.c: The seal assembly must be immediately replaced to prevent the inner pane from cracking

questions.justification: Page 3 indicates that the inner pane is able to maintain cabin pressure in case of outer pane failure, which is the core of the failsafe design.

questions.question: During the installation of a door window assembly, which sequence is correct for securing the panes?

options.a: Seal, followed by outer pane, then inner pane, secured by the retainer
options.b: Retainer, followed by inner pane, then seal, then outer pane
options.c: Outer pane, followed by the seal, then inner pane, then the retainer

questions.justification: The exploded view of the door window structure layout (page 4) shows the sequence: Window frame, sealing ring, panes (outer then inner), and finally the retainer.

questions.question: A technician finds moisture between the window panes. Which component failure most likely caused this condition?

options.a: A blocked vent hole in the inner pane
options.b: Failure of the retainer ring eye bolts
options.c: A crack in the outer pane fuselage skin interface

questions.justification: The vent hole (page 1) allows pressure equalization and moisture control between panes. If it is blocked, moisture can become trapped between the inner and outer panes.

questions.question: When replacing a cabin window panel assembly, how is the assembly interface with the fuselage skin sealed?

options.a: By applying a specific aerodynamic sealant around the eye bolts
options.b: By a dedicated seal that sits between the window frame and the panes
options.c: By the mechanical pressure of the retainer ring alone

questions.justification: The typical cross-section (page 1) shows a 'SEAL' component situated between the window frame/fuselage skin and the window panes.

questions.question: If an eye bolt is over-torqued during window installation, what is the most likely structural damage?

options.b: Cracking of the inner pane vent hole

questions.justification: The eye bolts attach directly to the window frame (page 1). Over-torquing transmits excessive stress to the frame itself rather than the acrylic panes.

questions.question: In the wing root joint assembly, which component acts as a safety feature for the bottom skin panel junction?

options.b: Safety butt-strap fitting

questions.justification: Page 13 explains that a 'lower triform fitting and a safety butt-strap fitting' make the junction between the center and outer wing box bottom skin panels.

questions.question: Which four structural elements are joined by the upper cruciform fitting at the wing root?

options.a: Center top skin, outer top skin, fuselage, and Rib 1
options.b: Front spar, rear spar, center bottom skin, and Rib 1

questions.question: During a structural repair of the center wing box, why is the Rib 1 datum critical?

options.a: It defines the location of the Main Landing Gear attachment point

questions.justification: The diagram on page 14 identifies the 'RIB 1 DATUM' at the intersection where the cruciform and triform fittings join the center and outer wing boxes.

options.a: At the intersection of the front spar and Rib 1

options.b: Three top skin panels and two bottom skin panels

questions.question: Where is the false rear spar attachment for the Main Landing Gear (MLG) located?

questions.question: During a borescope inspection through an access hole, you identify a 'Typical Stringer Shape'. How is this stringer attached to the skin?

options.a: Integral machining with the skin panel
options.b: Riveted to the skin using aluminum alloy butt straps

questions.justification: The diagram on page 21 shows the stringers as part of the 'Aluminium Alloy Skin Panels' and describes them as 'machined from aluminum alloy' on page 20.

questions.question: Where is the rear spar jointed in the outer wing box structure?

options.b: At Rib 6 and Rib 22
options.c: Continuously from Rib 1 to Rib 27 with no joints

questions.justification: The diagram on page 19 identifies specific 'REAR SPAR JOINT AT RIB 6' and 'REAR SPAR JOINT AT RIB 22'.

questions.question: What material and construction method are used for the bottom surface access panels of the fixed leading edge?

options.a: Solid aluminum alloy with flush rivets
options.b: CFRP sandwich construction with quick release fasteners

questions.justification: Page 29 states that bottom surface access panels are made of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Plastic (CFRP) sandwich construction and are attached with quick release fasteners.

questions.question: What is the power rating and frequency of the engine-driven Integrated Drive Generators (IDG)?

options.b: 90 kVA, 400 Hz

questions.justification: Page 64 lists the characteristics for engine generators as 115/200 volts, three phase, 400 Hz, 90 kVA.

questions.question: In the event of a failure of all main aircraft generators, what provides emergency AC power?

options.a: The static inverter supplied by Battery 1

questions.justification: Page 64 states that an AC emergency GEN is driven by the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) hydraulic circuit and automatically provides power in case of failure of all main generators.

questions.question: What is the specific order of priority for supplying AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2?

options.a: 1: APU GEN, 2: External Power, 3: Onside IDG, 4: Offside IDG
options.b: 1: Onside IDG, 2: External Power, 3: APU GEN, 4: Offside IDG

questions.question: Which component allows AC buses to be supplied by different power sources without parallel connection?

options.b: Bus Tie Contactors (BTCs)

questions.justification: Page 64 explains that the AC transfer circuit enables the AC BUS to be supplied by any generator via Bus Tie Contactors (BTCs), and generators are never connected in parallel.

questions.question: What is the maximum output current for each of the three identical Transformer Rectifiers (TRs)?
questions.justification: Page 65 states all TR characteristics include a maximum output of 200 A at 28V DC.

questions.question: The IDG oil outlet temperature has reached 142°C. What will be the indication on the flight deck?

options.a: The Master Caution will be triggered with a manual disconnect message
options.b: An advisory mode is available on the lower ECAM

questions.justification: Page 89 states: 'When the oil outlet temperature reaches 142°C, an advisory mode is available on the lower ECAM.'

questions.question: At what temperature does an automatic thermal disconnection of the IDG occur if the crew does not perform a manual disconnect?
questions.justification: Page 89 states: 'If the IDG disconnection is not performed at 185°C... at 200°C an automatic thermal disconnection should occur to protect the IDG.'

questions.question: A low IDG oil pressure condition is detected (below 140 psi) while the engine is running above underspeed. What is the status of the IDG FAULT light?

options.a: The FAULT legend comes on amber on the IDG pushbutton
options.b: The FAULT legend remains off because the engine is not underspeed
options.c: The light flashes white to indicate an advisory condition

options.c: To prevent the solder fuse from melting during the test

questions.justification: Page 102 states: 'Notice that for a static test of the IDG disconnect mechanism, the circuit breaker 2XU1 must be pulled to simulate a running engine 1 and no underspeed.'

options.a: It is reset automatically once the oil temperature drops below 100°C
options.b: The crew must cycle the GEN pushbutton OFF then ON

options.b: Flight Warning Computer (FWC)

questions.justification: Page 338 states: 'Each FWC generates all warning and caution messages...'

options.a: DMC 3 immediately takes over all six displays
options.b: DMC 2 automatically replaces DMC 1 for ECAM only
options.c: The ECAM displays go black and must be manually switched

questions.question: The ECAM system divides a flight into how many distinct flight phases for automatic page display?

options.b: 10 phases

questions.justification: Page 368 states: 'A flight is divided into 10 phases corresponding to an aircraft configuration change.'

questions.question: During a dual ECAM DU failure, how can the flight crew still view specific system pages?

options.a: By using the switching panel to transfer ECAM data to the PFD units
options.b: By rotating the ECAM/ND transfer selector to present EWD on the ND and holding a system key on the ECP
options.c: By accessing the MCDU MENU and selecting the system page on the scratchpad

questions.justification: Page 426 and 428 explain that in case of EWD and SD failure, the crew can present EWD on the ND unit and still recover system pages by pushing and holding a system key on the ECP.

questions.question: A level 3 ECAM alert is triggered. What are the specific aural and visual indications?

options.a: Single Chime, Master Caution light amber, and amber warning message
options.b: Continuous Repetitive Chime (CRC), Master Warning light flashing red, and red warning message
options.c: Specific sound, Master Warning light steady red, and no message on EWD

questions.justification: Page 372 describes Level 3 warnings as being associated with Continuous Repetitive Chime (CRC), red warning messages, and Master Warning light flashing red.

questions.question: The 'ADV' symbol is flashing on the lower part of the EWD. What does this indicate in a normal dual display configuration?

options.a: A critical system failure has occurred but the SD is displaying the wrong page
options.b: A parameter on a system page not currently displayed has drifted out of its normal range
options.c: The ECAM system is in maintenance mode and recording BITE data

questions.justification: Page 376 states the flashing ADV symbol appears when there is an advisory on an SD page other than the one currently displayed or selected.

questions.question: Following a total loss of both SDACs, which ECAM page data remains available to the crew?

options.a: No system pages are available as all sensors route through the SDACs
options.b: Only the CRUISE page is available as it is generated directly by the FWCs

questions.justification: Page 434 states that in case of SDAC 1+2 failure, 'ENG, FUEL, F/CTL and WHEEL ECAM page data is available because it is already in ARINC 429 format and not affected by SDAC failure.'

questions.question: What is the consequence of a failure of both Flight Warning Computers (FWCs)?

options.a: The ECAM displays will switch to a backup digital format directly from the sensors
options.b: All EWD messages, aural warnings, and attention getters are lost
options.c: Only red warnings are lost, but amber cautions remain available via the SDACs

questions.justification: Page 436 explains that if the DMCs receive no valid data from both FWCs, 'All other EWD messages, aural warnings and attention getters are lost.'

questions.question: Which control switch and position must be selected to turn on the logo lights and the first set of navigation lights?

questions.question: Where are the runway turn-off lights located on the aircraft?

options.a: On the leading edge of each wing root

options.c: The Ground/Flight logic must be in Ground mode

options.c: Either engine running and Master Switch ON

options.c: The duration of one full flight cycle

options.b: The internal batteries continue to supply the loads for at least 10 minutes
options.c: The emergency lights are shed to protect the main batteries

questions.justification: Page 645 states: 'If the 28V DC SHED ESS BUS voltage falls below 16V, the EPSUs internal batteries continue to supply the loads for at least 10 minutes.'

questions.question: Which busbar is the only one remaining serviceable to supply the ANN LTs in the event of an emergency electrical configuration?

options.b: 801XP (ESS)

questions.question: What triggers the automatic illumination of the exit marking signs and exit location signs independently of switch positions?

options.b: Excessive cabin depressurization
options.c: Total loss of AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2

questions.justification: Page 645 states: 'In the event of excessive cabin depressurization, the exit marking signs and the exit location signs automatically come on.'

questions.question: What are the primary components that constitute an Integrated Drive Generator (IDG)?

options.a: A Constant Speed Drive (CSD) and an AC generator
options.b: An air-driven turbine and a DC generator
options.c: A step-up gearbox and a permanent magnet alternator

questions.question: Where is the IDG oil filter Differential Pressure Indicator (DPI) located?

options.b: To regulate the fuel flow through the IDG heat management system
options.c: To increase oil pressure for the hydraulic trim unit

questions.question: Which component in the IDG scavenge line provides a visual indication of a clogged filter?

options.b: The pop-out Differential Pressure Indicator (DPI)
options.c: The internal scavenge pump relief valve

questions.justification: According to the cooling system description, a clogged filter indication is provided by a local visual Delta Pressure pop-out Indicator (DPI).

questions.question: In the IDG speed control loop, what is used as the frequency reference for the GCU control circuit?

options.b: The Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) frequency
options.c: The AC Essential Bus phase reference

questions.question: While monitoring the ECAM ELEC page, you observe that the IDG oil outlet temperature is 185°C. What action is required?

options.a: The IDG must be manually disconnected immediately
options.b: No action is required as automatic thermal disconnection occurs at 185°C
options.c: The related engine must be shut down to allow the IDG to cool

questions.justification: The document states if the oil outlet temperature is equal to or more than 185°C, the master caution is triggered and a manual disconnection is required.

questions.question: What condition must be met to allow a manual disconnection of the IDG via the IDG pushbutton switch?

options.a: The aircraft must be on the ground with engines shut down
options.b: The related engine must be running above underspeed
options.c: The IDG oil temperature must be below 142°C

questions.justification: Disconnection is only possible if the related engine is running above underspeed. An underspeed condition inhibits the manual disconnection.

questions.question: During IDG oil servicing, what is the importance of the drain hose status?

options.a: The drain hose must be removed immediately after the sight glass shows green
options.b: The drain hose should remain attached until only a couple of drops come out to avoid over-servicing
options.c: The drain hose must be pressurized to 35 PSI to clear air from the cooler

questions.justification: The maintenance tips specify that the most typical reason for IDG failures is over-servicing; therefore, leave the drain hose attached until only a couple of drops come out.

questions.question: What are the triggers for the amber FAULT legend on the IDG pushbutton switch?

options.a: IDG oil outlet temperature >185°C or oil pressure <140 psi (not caused by underspeed)
options.b: IDG oil outlet temperature >142°C or any differential current detection
options.c: IDG oil inlet temperature >105°C or engine speed below idle

questions.justification: The IDG P/B FAULT legend comes on if the IDG oil pressure is less than 140 psi or if the IDG oil outlet temperature is above 185°C. In underspeed conditions, the FAULT light remains off.

questions.question: After an automatic thermal disconnection of an IDG has occurred, what is the maintenance requirement?

options.a: The IDG can be reset by pulling the reset ring once cooled
options.b: The IDG must be replaced
options.c: Only the solder fuse must be replaced before the next flight

questions.justification: The document explicitly states: 'After a thermal disconnection, the IDG must be replaced.'

questions.question: Which unit is responsible for the regulation of generator voltage and frequency?

options.b: GCU
