questions.question: What determines the position and aircraft type configuration for a specific GCU?

options.a: Software upload via the PCMCIA card
options.b: Pin programming on the unit connector
options.c: Manual entry via the MCDU MENU

questions.justification: The general description of the GCU states that 'Pin programming provides the GCU with the following information: the aircraft type, the GCU position...'

questions.question: How does the GCU receive engine speed information for underspeed protection?

options.a: Directly from the Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) only
options.b: From the FADEC via an ARINC 429 bus
options.c: Via a dedicated discrete tachometer signal

questions.justification: The GCU receives engine speed data from the Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) via an ARINC 429 bus. PMG frequency is a back-up if FADEC data is unavailable.

questions.question: Where is the Point of Regulation (POR) monitored by the GCU located?

options.a: Directly at the IDG output stator
options.b: Between the 3-hole Current Transformer (CT) and the Generator Line Contactor (GLC)
options.c: At the AC Bus 1 tie point

questions.justification: The POR is located between the 3-hole CT and the GLC to account for generator feeder impedance voltage drops.

questions.question: Which internal GCU relay is responsible for connecting power to the Generator Line Contactor (GLC)?

options.b: Power Ready Relay (PRR)

questions.justification: The document states that 'The Power Ready Relay (PRR) controls the GLC.'

questions.question: A GCU has tripped due to an overvoltage fault (POR phase reached 130V AC). How is this fault reset?

options.a: By cycling the GEN pushbutton switch OFF then ON
options.b: By performing a cold reset of the aircraft electrical network
options.c: It resets automatically once the voltage returns to 115V AC

questions.justification: Under IDG monitoring/Generator P/BSW, it is stated that cycling the GEN switch resets the GCU after fault detection (tripping of the generator).

questions.question: What is the consequence of an open circuit in the IDG oil outlet temperature sensor?

options.a: An ECAM MASTER CAUTION is triggered immediately
options.b: It is a Class 3 fault with no flight deck effects
options.c: The IDG will be automatically disconnected by the GCU

questions.justification: The document notes: 'An open circuit of the IDG oil outlet temperature sensor is a class 3 fault, and no flight deck effects are presented.'

questions.question: Which protection provided by the GCU involves comparing the Line 3-hole CT and the CTs inside the IDG?

options.b: Differential Current Protection

questions.justification: Differential Protection is based on the comparison of each phase of the Line 3-hole CT and the CTs in the IDG. If the flow is above 50 +/- 10A, the relays trip.

questions.question: During engine start, the GEN FAULT light is ON. Is this considered a system failure?

options.a: Yes, it indicates a startup failure of the GCR
options.b: No, the FAULT lighting is normal when the engine is not running and voltage/frequency are out of tolerance
options.c: Yes, it indicates an underspeed condition detected by the FADEC

questions.justification: As per the Operation section, the PRR is de-energized when voltage and frequency are not in tolerance (engine not running), making the FAULT light normal until the engine is started.

questions.question: If Differential Current Protection trips, how many reset attempts are allowed via the GEN P/BSW before a cold reset is required?

options.b: Two attempts

questions.justification: The document states that Differential Protection circuit reset via GEN P/BSW is limited to two attempts, after which a cold reset must be performed.

questions.question: How are the main alternating current busbars identified in the aircraft electrical system?

options.a: Using the prefix PP followed by a sequence number
options.b: Using the prefix XP followed by a sequence number
options.c: Using the prefix AC followed by the engine number

questions.justification: According to the Main Busbar Identification section, letters XP are used for AC busbars and PP for DC busbars.

questions.question: Which bus is used specifically to supply 26V-400 Hz distribution?

options.a: Sub-busbars with the numbering sequence in the thirties (e.g., 131XP)
options.b: The Essential Transformer Rectifier (ESS TR) output

questions.justification: The document specifies that for the AC network, the thirties are used for the 26V-400 Hz distribution (e.g., 131XP).

questions.question: What characterizes a 'Virtual Busbar' in the aircraft schematic representations?

options.a: It is a busbar that only exists during emergency configurations
options.b: It identifies circuit breakers directly connected to the power source with letters IW
options.c: It is a software-simulated bus used by the DMCs for system monitoring

questions.justification: The section on Virtual Busbar Identification explains that some circuit breakers directly connected to the power source appear as virtual busbars identified by the letters IW.

questions.question: Which bus is normally supplied by AC BUS 1 or by AC BUS 2 if AC BUS 1 fails?

options.b: AC Ground Flight Bus

questions.justification: Under AC ESS BUS description, it is normally supplied by AC BUS 1 or by AC BUS 2 if AC BUS 1 fails.

questions.question: How are Ground/Flight (GND/FLT) buses supplied when External Power is connected but upstream of the EPC?

options.a: They cannot be supplied until the EPC is closed
options.b: They are supplied directly by the external power unit without energizing the whole network
options.c: They are supplied by the Static Inverter via the BAT BUS

questions.justification: The document states Ground/Flight buses are supplied directly by the external power unit, upstream of the EPC, without energizing the whole aircraft network.

questions.question: In the event of an AC BUS 1 loss, how long is the time delay before the automatic switching to AC BUS 2 occurs?

options.b: 3 seconds

questions.justification: Under AC BUS 1 LOSS logic, it specifies that 'after 3 seconds (17 XC time delay), 3XC2 is energized' to recover the AC ESS network from AC BUS 2.

questions.question: If AC BUS 1 is recovered after an automatic transfer of the Essential Bus to AC BUS 2, and airspeed is > 50 knots, what must the crew do to return to normal configuration?

options.b: Cycle the AC ESS FEED pushbutton switch
options.c: Reset the GCU 1 via the GEN 1 P/BSW

questions.justification: The document states: 'If the AC BUS 1 is recovered, AC ESS BUS remains on AC BUS 2. If the AC ESS FEED P/BSW 11XC is cycled... AC ESS BUS will switch back to the AC BUS 1.'

questions.question: What triggers the 'FAULT' legend on the AC ESS FEED pushbutton switch?

options.a: Loss of AC BUS 1 and failure of the automatic switching function (17XC relay)
options.b: Any overload on the AC Essential Sheddable Bus
options.c: Manual selection of the ALTN position on the switching panel

questions.justification: Under 'AUTO SWITCHING FAULT', it is stated that in case of automatic switching failure (17 XC failure), AC ESS BUS is no longer supplied and the FAULT legend on 11XC comes on.

questions.question: Which relays control the supply to the AC and DC ESS Sheddable buses during a battery-only emergency configuration?

options.b: Relays 2XB and 6XB, which remain closed

questions.justification: In a battery-only emergency configuration, the AC and DC SHED BUS are not supplied because relays 8XH and 8PH are open due to the fact that BATTERY ONLY relays 2XB and 6XB are energized.

questions.question: Following a TR 2 failure with External Power ON, how are the GND/FLT buses supplied?

options.a: They are lost because TR 2 is the only source for these buses
options.b: They are automatically supplied from TR 1 via DC BUS 1, battery BUS and DC BUS 2
options.c: They are supplied by the Static Inverter using Battery 2

questions.justification: Under 'TR2 FAILURE WITH EXT PWR ON', the document states that if TR2 fails, the GND/FLT buses are automatically supplied from TR1 via DC BUS 1, battery BUS and DC BUS 2.

questions.question: What is the capacity and nominal voltage of each of the two main batteries?

options.b: 15 Ah, 28V DC

questions.justification: Page 65 and 295 both state the battery capacity is 23 Ah with a nominal voltage of 24V DC.

questions.question: Which components are used to control the battery contactors for charging and protection?

options.b: Transformer Rectifiers (TRs)
options.c: Ground and Auxiliary Power Control Units (GAPCUs)

questions.justification: Page 271 states that BAT 1 and BAT 2 are charged from DC BAT BUS through contactors controlled by the Battery Charge Limiters (BCLs).

questions.question: Under what condition does the BCL connect a battery to the DC BAT BUS for charging?

options.a: When battery voltage is < 26.5V DC and BAT BUS voltage is > 27V DC
options.b: Whenever the engine generators are online
options.c: Only when the aircraft is on the ground

questions.justification: Page 301 states: 'When battery voltage is lower than 26.5V DC and BAT BUS voltage is higher than 27V DC... the battery is connected via contactor 6PB1.'

questions.question: What is the primary function of the HOT BUS 1 and HOT BUS 2?

options.a: To supply power to the IDG oil heaters
options.b: To provide permanently supplied power directly from the batteries
options.c: To supply high current for APU starting only

questions.justification: Page 65 states: 'Each battery has its own bus, HOT BUS 1 and HOT BUS 2. They are permanently supplied.'

questions.question: What logic does the BCL use to stop a battery charging cycle?

options.a: When battery voltage reaches exactly 28.5V DC
options.b: When charge current is < 4A for 10 seconds on ground or 30 minutes in flight
options.c: When the APU Master Switch is selected OFF

questions.justification: Page 301 explains that the charging stops when 'the charge current sensed by the battery shunt is less than 4 A decreasing for 10 s on ground or 30 min in flight.'

questions.question: On the ground, what happens if the battery voltage drops below 23V DC for more than 15 seconds?

options.a: The BCL automatically opens the battery contactor to prevent complete discharge
options.b: The APU automatically starts to recharge the batteries
options.c: The ECAM triggers a red WARNING and inhibits the DC Essential Bus

questions.justification: Page 301 states: 'On ground, when the battery voltage is lower than 23V DC for 15 s, the BCL supply contactor opens automatically.'

questions.question: How does the BCL protect the battery against a thermal runaway condition?

options.a: By increasing the charging voltage to 32V DC to reverse the chemical reaction
options.b: By opening the contactor if charge current is >10A and increasing by >0.375A/min
options.c: By automatically activating the battery compartment ventilation fans

questions.justification: Under 'THERMAL RUNAWAY OR SHORT CIRCUIT PROTECTION' on page 301, the BCL opens the contactor if charge current is above 10A and increasing by more than 0.375A per minute.

questions.question: To maintain the integrity of the HOT BUS supply, under what discharge current condition will the BCL open contactor 6PB1?

options.b: Discharge current > 50 A for 2 seconds

questions.justification: Page 301 specifies that contactor 6PB1 opens if discharge current is greater than 100 A for 300 ms or greater than 400 A for 5 ms.

questions.question: During an APU start on batteries, what is the role of the BCL regarding the DC BAT BUS?

options.a: The BCL isolates the batteries to protect them from high starter demand
options.b: The BCL connects both batteries to the 28V DC BAT BUS to withstand the high motor demand
options.c: The BCL limits the current to 100A to prevent battery fuse blowing

questions.justification: Page 303 explains: 'When the APU start sequence is initiated... batteries are connected to 28V DC BAT BUS in order to withstand the high APU starter motor demand.'

questions.question: In an electrical emergency configuration after landing, at what airspeed are the battery contactors closed by the BCLs?

options.b: Lower than 100 knots

questions.justification: Page 301 states: 'The battery contactors 6PB1 and 6PB2 are closed by BCLs when the aircraft speed is lower than 100 kts.'

questions.question: Where is the external power (EXT PWR) receptacle located on the aircraft?

options.a: Forward of the nose landing gear well
options.b: Aft of the left main landing gear well

questions.justification: Page 129 states the receptacle is 'located forward of the nose landing gear well.'

questions.question: Which unit controls and protects the connection of the Ground Power Unit (GPU) to the network?

options.b: The Ground and Auxiliary Power Control Unit (GAPCU)

questions.justification: Page 133 specifies that a 'Ground and Auxiliary Power Control Unit (GAPCU) controls and protects the connection and disconnection of the GPU.'

questions.question: What is indicated by the 'AVAIL' light on the EXT PWR pushbutton switch and the external power panel?

options.a: The External Power Contactor (EPC) is closed
options.b: The external power parameters (voltage/frequency) are correct and within limits
options.c: The ground cart is connected but its power is of poor quality

questions.justification: Page 131 explains that if external power parameters are correct, the indicator lights on the panel and the AVAIL light on the switch come on.

questions.question: Which relay within the GAPCU monitors the interlock voltage and quality of the ground power?

options.b: Generator Control Relay (GCR)

questions.justification: Page 133 describes that monitoring and control are made by two internal relays: the IMR and the Power Ready Relay (PRR).

questions.question: What happens if a short circuit occurs on the PRR output line sensed by the Positive Temperature Coefficient (PTC) sensor?

options.a: The red PTC TRIP LED on the front face of the GAPCU comes on
options.b: The EPC closes automatically to clear the fault through the main buses
options.c: The AC Essential Bus is immediately disconnected from the network

questions.justification: Page 133 states: 'If a short circuit occurs on the PRR output line... the red PTC TRIP LED on the front face of the GAPCU comes on.'

questions.question: What is the Over Voltage (OV) protection threshold and logic for external power as monitored by the GAPCU?

options.b: Highest phase voltage exceeds 130 +/- 1.5V AC followed by an inverse delay
options.c: Lowest phase voltage drops below 90V AC for 100ms

questions.justification: Page 138 states: 'An OV condition exists when the highest phase voltage exceeds 130 +/- 1.5V AC. After an inverse delay, the IMR, PRR and EPC are tripped.'

questions.question: Under what condition will the GAPCU trip the external power due to an Under Voltage (UV) condition?

options.a: Lowest phase voltage is < 101.5 +/- 1.5V AC for a maximum of 4.5 seconds
options.b: Any phase voltage is < 115V AC for more than 10 seconds
options.c: The interlock voltage drops below 28V DC

questions.justification: Page 138 specifies that an UV condition exists when the lowest phase voltage is less than 101.5 +/- 1.5V AC for 4.5 seconds max.

questions.question: The PTC LED on the GAPCU is illuminated. When will this LED turn off?

options.a: As soon as the external power is removed from the receptacle
options.b: After the crew cycles the EXT PWR switch ON/OFF
options.c: Only after a manual reset of the BCL units

questions.justification: Page 138 states: 'The LED is not a "latched" status signal. Thus... it will go off as soon as the external power is removed from the receptacle.'

questions.question: During a GAPCU failure, the back-up card allows connection of external power. What is the operational limitation in this mode?

options.a: Power is supplied with limited protection and no BITE function is available
options.b: The APU generator cannot be used simultaneously
options.c: The frequency is limited to 360 Hz to protect the transformers

questions.justification: Page 137 explains: 'In some GAPCU failure conditions... after a "cold reset" the PRR closes and external power is supplied... with limited protection. In that case, no bite function is available.'

questions.question: What is the priority logic between External Power and the APU Generator when both are available on the ground?

options.a: APU Generator has priority over External Power
options.b: External Power has priority over the APU Generator
options.c: They are connected in parallel to supply both AC buses

questions.justification: Page 137 states: 'The EPC AUX relay is also responsible for the priority switching, i.e. the External Power over the APU GEN.'

questions.question: Is the APU generator interchangeable with the Integrated Drive Generators (IDGs)?

options.a: Yes, they are identical in every A320 configuration
options.b: No, the APU generator is not interchangeable with the IDGs
options.c: Yes, provided the specific cooling adapter is used

questions.justification: Page 119 and 121 both state: 'The APU generator is not interchangeable with the Integrated Drive Generators (IDGs).'

questions.question: What provides the speed regulation for the APU generator to maintain a constant output frequency?

options.b: The APU engine (Electronic Control Box - ECB)
options.c: A mechanical governor in the APU gearbox

questions.justification: Page 121 states: 'Speed regulation is made by the APU engine without a Constant Speed Drive (CSD)' and 'APU ECB carries out the speed regulation.'

questions.question: At what RPM does the APU ECB send the 'APU READY' signal to the GAPCU?

options.b: 95% RPM

questions.justification: Page 121 specifies: 'At 95% rpm, the ECB sends an APU ready signal to the GAPCU.'

questions.question: Where are the APU generator feeder cables routed from the APU to the rear C/B panel?

options.a: Through the cargo floor belly structure
options.b: Through the cabin ceiling
options.c: Outside the fuselage in a dedicated conduit

questions.justification: Page 122 states: 'The feeder cables are routed through the cabin ceiling to the rear C/B panel in the cockpit.'

questions.question: What component within the APU oil system leads to an immediate automatic shutdown of the APU if high temperature is detected?

options.a: An oil temperature sensor on the generator oil outlet port
options.b: A pressure switch in the APU scavenge filter
options.c: A thermistor in the fuel/oil heat exchanger

questions.justification: Page 119 and 121 state that a high oil temperature (above 185°C) detected on the generator oil outlet port leads to an immediate shutdown via the ECB.

questions.question: The APU is running and the APU GEN switch is ON, but the APU is not supplying the network. No other power sources are available. What is the most likely cause?

options.a: The EPC AUX relay is energized (ground electrical power connected)
options.b: The aircraft is in flight and airspeed is above 100 knots
options.c: The IDG 1 and IDG 2 GLCs are energized

questions.justification: Page 122 explains that APU GLC voltage supply is interrupted if the EPC AUX is energized (indicating ground power is available).

questions.question: Under what condition will the APU Generator Line Contactor (AGLC) close to connect the generator to the transfer line?

options.a: Only if both engine generators are offline
options.b: If all generator parameters are correct and the GAPCU/bus tie logic authorize it
options.c: Automatically 10 seconds after the APU reaches 95% RPM regardless of other sources

questions.justification: Page 121 states: 'If all generator parameters are correct, the AGLC connects the generator to the transfer line. The connection to the busbars depends on the priority logic.'

questions.question: If the APU generator trips due to a fault, how is the system reset?

options.a: By cycling the APU GEN pushbutton switch to OFF and back to ON
options.b: By shutting down and restarting the APU
options.c: By performing a cold reset of the GAPCU through the MCDU

questions.justification: Page 121 states: 'After a fault detection... the GAPCU must be reset by setting the switch to OFF and back to ON.'

questions.question: What is the result of an APU generator overload condition while on the ground?

options.a: An ECAM message is triggered but no shedding occurs
options.b: The APU generator automatically sheds all the galley power
options.c: The APU shuts down immediately to prevent generator damage

questions.justification: Page 170 states: 'On the ground, an APU generator overload automatically sheds all the galley power.'

questions.question: While on the ground with APU and GEN 2 running (EPC not energized), what is the status of the network supply?

options.b: APU supplies AC Bus 1 and GEN 2 supplies AC Bus 2
options.c: APU supplies both AC buses through the transfer network

questions.justification: Under 'APU AND GEN2 RUNNING' on page 125, it states the APU Generator now supplies AC Bus 1 through the transfer network, but not AC Bus 2 (which is supplied by GEN 2).

questions.question: What is the output power rating of the Constant Speed Motor/Generator (CSM/G)?

options.b: 90 kVA continuously

questions.justification: Page 186 lists the generator output characteristics for the CSM/G as 'output power: 5 kVA continuously.'

questions.question: What is the function of the Static Inverter (STAT INV)?

options.a: It transforms 28V DC from Battery 1 into 115V AC single-phase
options.b: It rectifies 115V AC into 28V DC for the Essential TR
options.c: It steps up 24V DC to 400V DC for APU starting

questions.justification: Page 224 states: 'A STATic INVerter transforms the direct current from battery 1 into a single-phase alternating current... 115V AC, 400 Hz.'

questions.question: In case of a total loss of main generators in flight, which source supplies the AC Essential Bus BEFORE the emergency generator comes online?

options.b: Battery 1 via the STAT INV

questions.justification: Page 74 specifies: 'before the emergency generator connection, battery 1 will supply the AC ESS BUS, via the STAT INV.'

questions.question: What triggers the automatic extension of the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) in flight?

options.a: Total loss of main generators and airspeed above 100 knots
options.b: Loss of AC BUS 1 only
options.c: Selection of EMER GEN TEST on the ground

questions.justification: Page 74 states: 'In flight, in case of total loss of all the main generators... When its parameters are correct and the speed is more than 100 knots, the emergency generator comes on line.' Page 200 details the automatic deployment logic.

questions.question: The CSM/G hydraulic motor is pressurized by which aircraft system?

options.b: Blue hydraulic system

questions.justification: Page 186 states: 'The hydraulic motor is pressurized by the blue hydraulic system through an integrated solenoid valve.'

questions.question: During an emergency generator operational test (EMER GEN TEST), which component simulates the loss of AC buses and a speed > 100 knots?

options.b: Relay 20XE

questions.justification: Page 213 explains: 'When the EMERgency GENerator test pushbutton 16XE is pressed in, relay 3PH energizes simulating a loss of AC BUS 1 and AC BUS 2 and a speed higher than 100 kts.'

questions.question: In the automatic RAT deployment sequence, how long after the relays 17XE/18XE are de-energized does the RAT extension solenoid 1 receive power?

options.b: 1 second

questions.justification: Page 200 states: 'Relay 20XE is then energized after 1 second. and +28VDC are supplied from the Hot Battery Bus to the RAT solenoid 1.'

questions.question: Following a successful automatic RAT deployment, after 6 seconds, what change occurs in the CSM/G control supply?

options.a: The supply switches from Battery 2 to the Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) of the CSM/G
options.b: The supply switches from the Essential TR to the AC Essential Bus
options.c: The solenoid control valve is deactivated to conserve hydraulic pressure

questions.justification: Page 200 explains: 'After 6 seconds, relay 22XE closes its contacts... the control supply voltage of the CSM/G solenoid valve is switched from Battery 2 to the Permanent Magnet Generator (PMG) of the CSM/G.'

questions.question: When the aircraft speed drops below 50 knots during an emergency configuration landing, what is the effect on the AC Essential Bus?

options.a: It is recovered by the APU Generator
options.b: It disconnects from the static inverter
options.c: It is supplied by Battery 2 until 0 knots

questions.justification: Page 74 states: 'When the speed drops below 50 knots, the AC ESS BUS disconnects from the static inverter.'

questions.question: What is the consequence of pressing the 'MAN ON' pushbutton switch on the hydraulic panel while the aircraft is in a 'cold' configuration on the ground?

options.b: The APU fuel pump starts automatically
options.c: The Blue pump overrides and pressurizes the system to 3000 PSI

questions.justification: Page 196 warns: 'If the MAN ON P/BSW is pressed in, the RAT extends, even in cold aircraft configuration.'

questions.question: Where are the three Display Management Computers (DMCs) physically located in the aircraft?

options.b: In the aft avionics rack

questions.justification: As indicated in the EIS architecture component location on page 340, the EIS computers, including the DMCs, are located in the aft avionics rack.

questions.question: Which EIS component is primarily responsible for acquiring data and generating the images seen on the Display Units (DUs)?

options.b: Display Management Computer (DMC)

questions.justification: Page 338 states that DMCs are data concentrators that receive data from sensors/systems and send them to the DUs, which generate the images.

questions.question: In a normal configuration, what is the specific display distribution for DMC 1?

options.a: Captain PFD, Captain ND, EWD, and SD
options.b: F/O PFD, F/O ND, and SD

questions.justification: Page 338 explains that in normal operation, DMC 1 drives the Captain PFD, Captain ND, Engine/Warning Display (EWD), and System Display (SD).

questions.question: What happens if DMC 1 fails regarding the ECAM displays (EWD and SD)?

options.a: DMC 3 must be manually selected immediately
options.b: DMC 2 automatically replaces DMC 1 to drive the ECAM displays
options.c: The displays are lost and cannot be recovered

questions.justification: Page 338 states: 'If DMC 1 fails, it is automatically replaced by DMC 2 for ECAM only.'

questions.question: Which data bus standard is used by the DMCs to transmit computed image data to the Display Units?

options.b: ARINC 629

questions.justification: Page 388 and 389 specify that DMCs send data to the DUs through ARINC 629 output buses.

questions.question: Following a total failure of DMC 1, what action must the Captain take to recover their Primary Flight Display (PFD)?

options.a: Nothing, the system performs an automatic transfer to DMC 2
options.b: Rotate the EIS DMC selector switch to the CAPT 3 position
options.c: Cycle the PFD/ND XFR pushbutton on the switching panel

questions.justification: Page 438 explains that if DMC 1 fails, the CAPT has to switch to DMC 3 by rotating the EIS DMC selector to CAPT 3 to recover the EFIS displays.

questions.question: During a manual reconfiguration where the EIS DMC switch is set to F/O 3, how is the data routed?

options.a: DMC 3 sends data directly to the F/O DUs
options.b: DMC 2 sends data through its output bus that was received from DMC 3
options.c: DMC 1 provides a cross-talk link to bypass the failed DMC 2

questions.justification: Page 406 states: 'When the EIS DMC Selector Switch is set to CAPT 3 (or F/O 3), DMC 1 (or DMC 2) sends through its output bus the data received from DMC3.'

questions.question: When installing a new Display Management Computer, what is the required maintenance procedure regarding software?

options.a: No action is needed as software is hard-coded in the DMC
options.b: The relevant software must be cross-loaded from an operational DMC via the MCDU
options.c: Software must be uploaded only via a floppy disk into the MDDU

questions.justification: Page 394 states: 'When a new DMC 1, 2 or 3 is installed, the relevant software must be downloaded into it, this is done by cross loading from DMC 1, 2 or 3 via the MCDU.'

questions.question: Which DMC port/interface is used for connecting a Portable Data Loader (PDL)?

options.a: ARINC 429 port on the rear rack
options.b: The test connector (RS 232) on the front panel of the unit
options.c: The Ethernet port on the cockpit center pedestal

questions.justification: Page 564 explains that to enable the connection of a PDL, a test connector is installed on the front panel of the computer, using an RS 232 interface.

questions.question: If both DMC 1 and DMC 2 fail, can DMC 3 drive the displays for both the Captain and First Officer simultaneously?

options.a: Yes, it acts as a universal hot spare for all six DUs
options.b: No, it can only be switched to drive either the Captain or the F/O side, not both
options.c: Only if the ECAM/ND XFR switch is in the NORM position

questions.justification: Page 338 states: 'DMC 3 can drive any of the six DUs. DMC 3 is a hot spare... and can be switched to drive the DUs linked to the failed DMC.' This implies it can supply either or both sides upon selection.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary output from the Flight Warning Computers (FWCs)?

options.b: Aural alerts and synthetic voice messages
options.c: Engine N1 and N2 digital signals

questions.justification: Page 309 states: 'The FWCs then supply... the loudspeakers with aural alerts and synthetic voice messages.'

questions.question: What is considered the 'heart' of the Electronic Centralized Aircraft Monitoring (ECAM) system?

options.b: The Flight Warning Computers (FWCs)

questions.justification: Page 309 explicitly refers to the FWCs as the 'heart of the ECAM system.'

questions.question: Which alert level corresponds to an abnormal configuration requiring immediate crew awareness, but not immediate corrective action?

options.b: Level 2

questions.justification: Page 372 describes Level 2 as agreeing with an abnormal configuration where immediate crew awareness is required, but not immediate corrective action.

questions.question: How are Level 3 warnings distinguished from Level 2 cautions in terms of audio signaling?

options.a: Level 3 uses a Continuous Repetitive Chime (CRC); Level 2 uses a Single Chime (SC)
options.b: Level 3 uses a Single Chime (SC); Level 2 uses a triple beep
options.c: Level 3 uses a buzzer; Level 2 uses a synthetic voice

questions.justification: Page 372 states Level 3 warnings use a CRC or specific sound, while Level 2 cautions use a Single Chime (SC).

questions.question: Which EIS component computes the flight phase (1 through 10) used for alert inhibition?

options.b: FWC

questions.justification: Page 386 states that the FWCs perform three main functions, including 'Flight phase computation.'

questions.question: What is the consequence of a failure of both Flight Warning Computers (FWC 1 + 2)?

options.a: All attention getters and aural warnings are lost, and only engine data is displayed
options.b: The SDACs take over alert generation using a backup protocol
options.c: The DMCs will generate text messages based on raw sensor data

questions.justification: Page 436 states that if DMCs receive no valid data from both FWCs, 'All other EWD messages, aural warnings and attention getters are lost.'

questions.question: During takeoff (Flight Phases 3, 4, and 5), most warnings are inhibited by the FWC. What message is displayed on the EWD to indicate this?

options.b: TO INHIBIT

questions.justification: Page 368 specifies that during engine phases 3, 4, and 5, 'TO INHIBIT is displayed on the right memo area of the EWD.'

questions.question: If FWC 1 fails, how is the alert data for the DMCs managed?

options.a: DMC 1 manually switches to SDAC 2 for warning data
options.b: The DMCs automatically switch to the FWC 2 data bus
options.c: The attention getters are disabled for the Captain's side

questions.justification: Page 402 explains: 'If the data is not valid or if FWC 1 is not valid, the DMCs will automatically switch to the FWC 2 Data bus.'

questions.question: Which flight phase is entered five minutes after the last engine shutdown?

options.b: Phase 1 (DOOR)

questions.justification: Page 368 states: 'Five minutes after the last engine shutdown the FWC starts a new flight leg at phase 1.'

questions.question: A Level 1 alert occurs in flight. What is the crew notification on the flight deck?

options.a: Master Caution light and Single Chime
options.b: Only warning messages on the LCD; no lights or sounds are activated
options.c: A white 'ADV' message flashing in the center of the EWD

questions.justification: Page 372 states that for Level 1 alerts, 'The attention getters (lights and sounds) are not activated by a level 1 alert.'

questions.question: What is the primary role of the System Data Acquisition Concentrators (SDACs)?

options.a: To generate audio for synthetic voice messages
options.b: To acquire aircraft system signals and distribute them to the FWCs and DMCs
options.c: To control the brightness of the Liquid Crystal Display units

questions.justification: Page 338 and 382 state that SDACs receive various signals from systems and send them to the FWCs (for alert generation) and DMCs (for display information).

questions.question: How many SDACs are installed in the A320 aircraft, and are they interchangeable?

options.b: Two, identical and interchangeable

questions.justification: Page 382 confirms: 'The two SDACs are identical and interchangeable.'

questions.question: Which of the following data formats entering the SDACs is converted into ARINC 429 digital format?

options.b: Discrete, analog, and digital signals
options.c: Only RS 232 serial signals from the MCDU

questions.justification: Page 384 states: 'All the signals (discrete, analog, digital) entering the SDACs are converted into digital format and delivered on their output buses under ARINC 429.'

questions.question: If SDAC 1 provides invalid data, what is the automatic system response?

options.a: The ECAM displays will switch to a backup analog mode
options.b: The DMCs will automatically use data from SDAC 2
options.c: The FWC will inhibit all amber cautions for the duration of the flight

questions.justification: Page 404 explains: 'If the data is not valid or if SDAC 1 is not valid, the DMCs will use the data from SDAC 2. The switching is automatic.'

questions.question: Which alert type is primarily generated by the FWCs using data acquired by the SDACs?

options.b: Amber cautions

questions.justification: Page 338 and 382 explain that inputs received by the SDACs are used by the FWCs to generate most amber warnings (cautions).

questions.question: Following a total loss of BOTH SDACs (FWS SDAC 1+2 FAULT), which information is lost on the ECAM?

options.b: All amber cautions and most system pages
options.c: All primary engine parameters and the EWD

questions.justification: Page 434 states: 'In case both SDACs fail the amber cautions and most of the system displays are lost.'

questions.question: Why does the 'WHEEL' ECAM page remain available even if both SDACs have failed?

options.a: It uses a dedicated analog backup link to the DMCs
options.b: The data is already in ARINC 429 format and not processed by the SDACs
options.c: It is driven directly by the landing gear LGCIU 2

questions.justification: Page 434 explains: 'ENG, FUEL, F/CTL and WHEEL ECAM page data is available because it is already in ARINC 429 format and not affected by SDAC failure.'

questions.question: A fault message 'FWS SDAC 1 FAULT' appears on the EWD. What is the operational consequence for the flight crew?

options.a: The aircraft must be diverted immediately to the nearest airfield
options.b: There is no operational consequence due to the redundancy of the EIS
options.c: The ECAM must be manually switched to mono-display mode

questions.justification: Page 434 specifies: 'In the case of a SDAC failure, there is no operational consequence due to the redundancy of the EIS.'

questions.question: Which unit digitizes the analog signal from the linear accelerometer before it is sent to the FDIU part of the FDIMU?

options.b: The SDAC

questions.justification: Page 328 states: 'The System Data Acquisition Concentrator (SDAC) digitizes the analog signal of the linear accelerometer and sends it to the FDIU.'

questions.question: During a 'FWS SDAC 1+2 FAULT' scenario, what instruction is provided to the crew via the EWD?

options.b: MONITOR OVERHEAD PANEL

questions.justification: According to the diagram on page 435, the EWD displays 'FWS SDAC 1+2 FAULT' with the instruction 'MONITOR OVERHEAD PANEL.'

questions.question: What is the main function of the Primary Flight Display (PFD)?

options.a: To show engine oil temperature and pressure
options.b: To provide flight information for A/C control, including attitude, airspeed, and altitude
options.c: To display the status of the electrical distribution network

questions.justification: Page 398 states: 'The PFDs provide flight information for A/C control, including A/C attitude, airspeed, altitude, heading and Automatic Flight System modes.'

questions.question: Where are the control knobs for adjusting the brightness (BRT) of the PFD and ND located?

options.b: Outboard of the PFD units on the main instrument panel

questions.justification: Page 315 states: 'Outboard of the PFDs, there are control knobs to adjust the brightness of the associated PFD and ND...'

questions.question: If the METRIC ALT pushbutton on the FCU is pressed, where is the altitude displayed in meters?

options.a: At the bottom of the System Display
options.b: Above the altitude scale on the PFD
options.c: Only on the MCDU PROG page

questions.justification: Page 398 specifies: 'If you push this pushbutton, the selected altitude is displayed in meters above the altitude scale.'

questions.question: What happens automatically if the PFD display unit itself fails (internal hardware fault)?

options.a: The image is automatically transferred to the EWD unit
options.b: The PFD image is automatically displayed on the ND unit
options.c: The system display (SD) is replaced by the PFD image

questions.justification: Page 412 states: 'In the case of PFD failure (detected)... the PFD is automatically displayed on the ND unit.'

questions.question: What area of the PFD displays the Automatic Flight System (AFS) modes?

options.b: The top area (Flight Mode Annunciator)
options.c: The vertical scale to the left of the attitude indicator

questions.justification: According to the PFD diagram on page 399, 'AFS MODES' are shown in the top header section (FMA area).

questions.question: Following an automatic transfer of the PFD to the ND unit, how can the crew manually recover the ND image?

options.a: By turning the EWD brightness knob to OFF
options.b: By pressing the PFD/ND XFR pushbutton switch
options.c: By selecting the PLAN mode on the EFIS control panel

questions.justification: Page 414 and 416 explain that the PFD/ND transfer (XFR) P/BSW provides the crew with the possibility to recover the ND image on the ND unit.

questions.question: If a PFD unit is switched off via its potentiometer, what is the resulting display configuration?

options.a: The DU remains black and no information is transferred
options.b: The PFD image is automatically transferred to the associated ND DU
options.c: The ND image is lost and the EWD takes over the Captain's PFD

questions.justification: Page 412 states: 'if the PFD unit is switched off by means of its potentiometer, the PFD is automatically displayed on the ND unit.'

questions.question: During troubleshooting, you see 'ATTITUDE' in red on the PFD. What action is recommended by the EWD?

options.a: Switch the ATT HDG selector to the opposite IR source
options.b: Cycle the DMC selector to CAPT 3
options.c: Reset the FWC circuit breakers on the overhead panel

questions.justification: Page 440 and 441 explain that in the case of external source failures (like attitude), the crew should follow EWD instructions, such as 'ATT HDG SWTG F/O' on the switching panel to recover info.

questions.question: Is it possible to display the System Display (SD) synoptic on the PFD unit during a multiple display failure?

options.a: Yes, by rotating the ECAM/ND transfer selector
options.b: No, the SD can be presented on the ND unit but never on the PFD side
options.c: Only if the aircraft is on the ground with engines shutdown

questions.justification: Page 424 specifies: 'Each crew member also has the possibility to present the SD image on the ND side only, and never on the PFD side...'

questions.question: What is the consequence on the PFD if Air Data/Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) information is lost?

options.a: The PFD will automatically switch to GPS backup data
options.b: The information (e.g. Attitude, Altitude) will appear in red on the PFD
options.c: The PFD image will turn white and flash 'DMC FAIL'

questions.justification: Page 440 states: 'In the case of external source information failures, the lost information appears in red on the PFD or ND.'

questions.question: Which of the following are valid display modes for the Navigation Display (ND)?

options.b: ROSE-NAV, ARC, and PLAN

questions.justification: Page 396 lists the ND modes as ROSE-ILS, ROSE-VOR, ROSE-NAV, ARC, and PLAN.

questions.question: Which data bus standard is used by the DMCs to receive Weather Radar (WXR) information?

options.b: ARINC 453

questions.justification: Page 394 and 408 state that DMCs receive weather radar information on the ARINC 453 high-speed bus.

questions.question: What happens to the Weather Radar (WXR) display on the ND if the PLAN mode is selected?

options.a: WXR is displayed only in the top right corner
options.b: A WXR enable discrete disables WXR operation in PLAN mode
options.c: WXR is automatically overlaid on the north-oriented map

questions.justification: Page 408 specifies: 'The WXR enable discrete disables the operation if the plan mode is selected on the EFIS controller.'

questions.question: How many Weather Radar transceivers (XCVRs) can be in operation and processed by the DMCs at one time?

options.b: Both simultaneously for redundancy

questions.justification: Page 408 states: 'As only one WXR XCVR is in operation at a time, the DMCs process information from the one in operation.'

questions.question: Which EIS computer retransmits the ARINC 453 weather bus to the EFIS Display Units?

options.a: The Flight Data Interface Management Unit (FDIMU)
options.b: The Display Management Computer (DMC)

questions.justification: Page 408 states: 'DMCs retransmit the ARINC 453 bus to the EFIS DUs.'

questions.question: A Captain ND failure occurs. How can the Captain view the ND image?

options.a: It automatically transfers to the F/O ND unit
options.b: By pressing the PFD/ND XFR pushbutton on the Captain's switching panel
options.c: By rotating the ECAM/ND XFR selector on the center pedestal

questions.justification: Page 416 states: 'In the case of ND unit failure the crew has the possibility to present the ND image [on the PFD unit] by pressing the PFD/ND XFR P/BSW.'

questions.question: When the PFD/ND XFR pushbutton is pressed following an ND failure, how long does the ND screen stay in place of the PFD screen?

options.b: Until the pushbutton is pressed again
options.c: Until the next flight phase transition

questions.justification: Page 418 states: 'The ND screen stays instead of the PFD screen until the PFD/ND XFR P/BSW is pressed again.'

questions.question: What determines if the ND displays magnetic or true heading in PLAN mode?

options.a: The selection made on the switching panel
options.b: The PLAN mode specifically displays True North (TN)
options.c: The selection on the Captain's EFIS control panel brightness knob

questions.justification: The ND diagram on page 397 shows the PLAN mode with 'TN' (True North) indicated in the bottom right corner.

questions.question: A technician is installing a new Display Unit (DU). What must be done regarding software initialization?

options.a: Manually enter the DU part number into the CFDIU
options.b: Perform a cross loading from the corresponding DMC via the MCDU
options.c: Nothing, the DU auto-calibrates to the DMC on power up

questions.justification: Page 394 states: 'When a new DU is installed, a cross loading from the corresponding DMC has to be performed via the MCDU.'

questions.question: Which EIS component re-transmits data from the Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning Computer (EGPWC) to the ND?

options.b: DMC

questions.justification: Page 408 specifies that each DMC receives the EGPWC data via four ARINC 453 data buses and retransmits it to the EFIS DUs.

questions.question: What information is permanently displayed on the UPPER area of the Engine/Warning Display (EWD)?

options.a: Primary engine parameters, FOB, and Slat/Flap position
options.b: Secondary engine parameters and electrical bus status

questions.justification: Page 342 states that primary engine parameters, slat/flap position, and Fuel On Board (FOB) are permanently displayed on the EWD upper area.

questions.question: What is the Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR) used for on the EWD?

options.a: It is a primary parameter for IAE engines
options.b: It is a secondary parameter for CFM engines only
options.c: It indicates the fuel flow pressure to the combustion chamber

questions.justification: Page 350 states: 'For an IAE engine, the parameters will be shown as follows: Engine Pressure Ratio (EPR), EGT, N1 and N2.'

questions.question: Which area of the EWD is dedicated to the display of memos, failure messages, and required crew actions?

options.b: The lower area

questions.justification: Page 342 states: 'On the lower area are displayed: Memos, failure messages and actions to be performed.'

questions.question: How are secondary failures (those resulting from a primary failure) indicated on the Engine/Warning Display?

options.a: With a box around the failure title
options.b: With an asterisk (*) on the lower right part of the display

questions.justification: Page 374 states: 'The titles of the system pages corresponding to the secondary failures are indicated on the lower right part of the Engine/Warning Display (EWD) by an asterisk.'

questions.question: What is the meaning of a box around a failure title on the ECAM EWD?

options.b: It indicates a primary failure causing the loss of other equipment
options.c: It indicates the failure has been cleared by the crew

questions.justification: Page 374 states: 'NOTE: A primary failure is displayed with a box around the failure.'

questions.question: A green overflow arrow appears at the bottom of the left memo area. What does this signify to the crew?

options.a: A secondary failure page is available for manual selection
options.b: Warning messages exceed the capacity of the display (more than 7 lines)
options.c: A critical parameter has reached its maximum peak value

questions.justification: Page 348 and 362 state: 'The overflow arrow in green color indicates that warning messages exceed the capacity of the display on the left memo area (7 lines).'

questions.question: In the case of an UPPER ECAM DU failure, what is the automatic system response?

options.a: The EWD image is automatically transferred to the lower display unit
options.b: The SD image is lost and only the EWD is displayed on the ND
options.c: Both displays go black and must be manually recovered using DMC 3

questions.justification: Page 420 states: 'In the case of an upper display (EWD) failure... the upper display is automatically transferred on the lower display.'

questions.question: How is a 'Status' reminder (STS) indicated on the EWD after a failure has been cleared?

options.a: A green box pulses at the top of the upper area
options.b: A white STS box appears at the bottom of the EWD
options.c: The MASTER CAUTION light flashes continuously

questions.justification: Page 356 and 357 state: 'When you press CLR a last time, the STATUS reminder STS on the EWD indicates that the STATUS page is not empty.'

questions.question: In ECAM mono-display mode, what happens if an aircraft system parameter drifts out of its normal operating range?

options.a: The related system page is automatically displayed on the ND
options.b: A white ADV message flashes in the center of the EWD
options.c: The EWD is inhibited until the crew clears the message

questions.justification: Page 378 specifies that in mono-display mode, 'a white ADV message flashes in the center of the EWD to attract crew attention.'

questions.question: What is the indication of an 'independent failure' on the EWD?

options.a: The failure title is enclosed in a box
options.b: The failure title is underlined
options.c: The failure title flashes in red only

questions.justification: Page 374 states: 'NOTE: An independent failure is displayed with the title underlined.'

questions.question: How many specific system synoptic pages can the System Display (SD) unit show?

options.b: 11 pages

questions.justification: Page 362 and 363 state: 'The SD can display one of 11 system pages...'

questions.question: Where is the permanent data (TAT, SAT, ISA, GMT, GW) located on the System Display (SD)?

options.b: In the lower area below the grey line
options.c: On the right hand column under INOP SYS

questions.justification: Page 362 and 363 state: 'the lower area is dedicated to permanent data' and 'At the bottom of the SD, below the grey line is the permanent data.'

questions.question: Which system page is automatically displayed in flight whenever no specific manual or failure mode is active?

options.b: CRUISE

questions.justification: Page 362 states: 'The CRUISE page is automatically displayed in flight (no manual selection).'

questions.question: Under what condition does the 'Advisory' mode automatically display a related system page in normal dual display operation?

options.a: When a level 3 warning is triggered
options.b: When a critical system parameter drifts out of its normal operating range
options.c: Immediately after the first engine start

questions.justification: Page 376 explains that when there is a deviation of a value from its normal range, 'the related system page is displayed automatically' in advisory mode.

questions.question: In the 'Status' page, what information is listed on the right hand side of the display?

options.b: Inoperative systems (INOP SYS) and maintenance failures

questions.justification: Page 311 and 362 state that the Status page displays 'INOPerative SYStem on the RH side' and 'any class 2 system failure below the caption "MAINTENANCE".'

questions.question: Following a 'lower display turned off' scenario, how can the crew view a specific system synoptic page (e.g. HYD)?

options.a: They cannot; the EWD permanently replaces the SD
options.b: By rotating the ECAM/ND transfer selector to CAPT or F/O to display it on the ND unit
options.c: By holding the ALL key on the ECP for 10 seconds

questions.justification: Page 424 and 425 explain that if the lower display is turned off, the crew can present the SD image on the ND side only by rotating the ECAM/ND transfer selector switch.

questions.question: During a flight phase 2 (WHEEL), what causes the WHEEL page to be replaced by the F/CTL page for 20 seconds?

options.a: When the aircraft speed exceeds 80 knots
options.b: When either sidestick is moved or rudder deflection is above 22 degrees
options.c: When the landing gear is retracted

questions.justification: Page 368 states: 'The FLighT ConTroL page replaces the WHEEL page for 20 seconds when either sidestick is moved or when rudder deflection is above 22 degrees.'

questions.question: A parameter on the System Display shows as two dashed lines (XX) in cyan. What does this signify?

options.b: The data is not available
options.c: The system is in maintenance mode

questions.justification: According to the diagram on page 364, values replaced by 'XX' signify 'DATA NOT AVAILABLE.'

questions.question: What is the priority order for system page presentation on the ECAM SD?

options.b: Normal, Failure, Advisory, Manual

questions.justification: Page 366 lists the priority order as: 1. Normal mode (flight phase), 2. Failure mode, 3. Advisory mode, 4. Manual mode.

questions.question: In the event of an ECAM Control Panel (ECP) failure, how can the crew scroll through all system pages?

options.a: By using the switching panel selector
options.b: By repeatedly pressing or holding the ALL key
options.c: By using the line select keys on the MCDU

questions.justification: Page 370 explains that in case of ECP failure, 'system pages are still available through the ALL key... When the ALL key is pressed and held, all the system pages are displayed successively.'
